scope: Optional conservative total-species and total-enthalpy flux reference BVP with full thermochemistry and multicomponent/Soret transport.
method: Optional interval total-species and total-enthalpy flux divergences on nodal dual volumes. Same full chemistry, multicomponent/Soret transport, free-flame continuity, temperature anchor, algebraic mass closure and BVP tolerances. Steady reference only; pseudo-time stabilization is not physical transient integration.

projection.allowance_basis: 10 times BVP absolute species tolerance plus 64*(N+1)*machine epsilon for closure arithmetic

interruption.action: SIGINT to the exact owned reference solver process after repeated unsuccessful steady Newton attempts; round closeout requested by user.

arithmetic_allowance.normalization: Each independently recomputed quantity divided by the sum of absolute constituent terms before any cancellation, with the same dual-volume/rho/cp factors.
arithmetic_allowance.purpose: Allow floating arithmetic and grouping differences between C++ and Python in recorded flux/equation consistency only, not combustion accuracy or residual convergence.
arithmetic_allowance.cost: O(points*species) arithmetic plus one thermodynamic query per node and one conductivity query per interval; no new nonlinear solve.

preserved_reader_failures.cause: Positional Python Cantera constructor silently selected mixture-averaged transport; corrected to named multicomponent model with an assertion.
Arithmetic denominator incorrectly used already-canceled total face flux. Corrected to the absolute advective plus diffusive constituent terms; unchanged epsilon multiplier and physical gates.

limits: Conservative upwind reference still has discretization error; speed and temperature sensitivity must be reported independently of flux closure.
This is an independent steady BVP algorithm sharing Cantera thermochemistry and collision data; it is not independent experimental validation.
Constant-pressure reference omits longitudinal kinetic energy and viscous work retained by native compressible flow.
The pseudo-time term stabilizes the BVP nonlinear solve and is not physical transient integration.
Raw negative BVP roundoff is retained; bounded preparation is only for new initial data, never a native accepted checkpoint.
Zero-time input readback does not establish native evolution or flame-speed accuracy.
